markdown_report:
The strongest early-stage proposal is **terminal candidate competition**: retain corrected BERT4Rec and replace only its terminal-branch loss with cross-entropy over one positive and 32 uniformly sampled negatives.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Appended-mask inference requires prediction from preceding observations. Terminal-prefix supervision matches this condition without revealing the target. (2) Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics have negative tenth-percentile margins and wrong-rank rates of 12.25% and 11.27%. These measured training-position errors motivate discrimination experiments, but do not establish validation performance. (3) Users report both broad resemblance displacing specific matches and historical interests displacing present priorities. Competition at terminal prefixes could address both indirectly; observed histories cannot establish current intent, compatibility or ownership.

**Insights from related work.** (1) BERT4Rec establishes bidirectional masked-item learning [1]. Candidate competition changes its objective while preserving the backbone. (2) Negative-sampling comparisons report dataset-dependent tradeoffs [2]. Uniform sampling is therefore a conservative first experiment rather than a claim that harder negatives always help. (3) PSL highlights false-negative sensitivity [3]. This motivates avoiding aggressive mining initially; the proposed loss is ordinary sampled cross-entropy, not PSL.

**Framework.** Three directions isolate different bottlenecks: objective competition changes which alternatives must be separated; temporal attention changes how history persists; text fusion changes which item attributes are represented. Their corresponding gaps are false negatives, unavailable target timestamps, and semantic resemblance substituting for behavioral relevance.

**Candidate assessments.** Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive and negative assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Terminal candidate competition | 3/7/6/8/3 | Established objective, but a useful controlled adaptation; promising and directly targets weak margins; user benefits remain indirect; small training change, with sampling checks required. |
| Bucketed temporal attention | 5/7/7/5/7 | Flexible persistence could address stale interests and broad historical associations; novelty is incremental, timestamps require careful handling, and margin benefits are unverified. |
| Jointly learned title encoder | 4/7/7/5/8 | Could represent specific attribute combinations and finer entertainment preferences; established fusion ideas, sparse text supervision, semantic shortcuts and export complexity limit confidence. |

**Selected experiment.** At 0% progress, candidate competition offers the clearest feasible intervention. Preserve existing terminal/interior sampling, branch weights and interior loss. Average terminal cross-entropy per example. Draw 32 unique negatives excluding reserved tokens, the target and observed training positives; retain every history item. This tests whether explicit alternatives reduce broad-match and stale-interest errors while improving weak margin tails; it does not directly solve incompatibility or duplication.

Use identical negative panels for diagnostic comparisons and report counts, margin definitions and unavailable fields. Select exclusively through the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10. Preserve seeds, routing, limits, diagnostic interfaces and one checkpoint per category. No inference change is needed; verify the existing writer reloads the exact trained architecture. References: [1–3] below.

idea.description: Terminal candidate competition within one corrected BERT4Rec per category: replace the existing terminal-prefix objective with uniform 32-negative sampled cross-entropy while preserving the interior masked-item objective, backbone, existing branch coefficients and appended-mask inference.
idea.motivation: The proposal explicitly targets two user-facing failures: broad associations outranking specific matches, and historical interests outranking recent priorities. Terminal prefixes contain the recent observed context, and candidate competition requires the selected target to beat multiple alternatives within that context. These mechanisms are hypotheses, not measurements of user intent. The model-facing target is weak positive–negative separation, particularly Industrial_and_Scientific's margin p10=-0.2872 and Electronics' p10=-0.1374. Embedding similarity near 0.5 does not motivate an anti-collapse intervention.
idea.implementation_notes:
Integrate the supplied loss helper into the corrected baseline; it is not a standalone replacement train.py because the baseline source and artifact interfaces were not supplied. The helper accepts terminal appended-mask features and already sampled candidate IDs, so it does not assume a particular model constructor or predictor signature.

Use K=32 unique uniformly sampled real-item negatives per terminal example, without replacement from the eligible catalog. Exclude PAD, MASK, target ID and all observed training positives for that user. Never inspect validation/test labels when constructing exclusions. If fewer than 32 eligible items exist, use all eligible items and PAD-fill the remaining candidate slots; the loss masks those slots. Fail explicitly if no eligible negative exists. This exclusion policy is part of the proposed sampling intervention; disclose any difference from baseline sampling. Unobserved candidates may still be relevant. This finite candidate objective does not claim unbiased full-softmax estimation and applies no sampling correction.

Keep terminal prefix construction leakage-free: choose the baseline endpoint, remove its target occurrence and every later interaction, truncate the preceding history to maxlen-1, append the reserved MASK, and left-pad. Earlier repeated target occurrences are legitimate history, even though the target ID is excluded from negative candidates. Do not provide target metadata or timestamps. Preserve the baseline interior masks, loss, branch allocation, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, validation cadence and checkpoint policy. Use the baseline branch coefficient rather than introducing another curriculum. Normalize the terminal loss across examples. Do not add protected-context dropout, hard mining, text features or temporal biases in this first experiment.

The code calls the actual model's log2feats and item_emb interfaces. Its dot-product scorer must match the corrected baseline's scorer; if the baseline applies a learned scoring transformation or bias, pass its canonical differentiable predict_score implementation as score_fn. Do not silently substitute dot products for a different scoring head. No independent popularity, transition or text scorer is introduced.

Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl; DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; preprocessing seed 0; training seed 42; at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Respect the environment's epoch default of 200. Train on one GPU and write artifacts beneath the trial directory. Train exactly one independent model per category in this trial, and export one selected checkpoint per route. Do not inspect other trials or reuse their checkpoints. All execution and diagnostics count against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Historical inspiration scores do not establish this objective's improvement.

Keep the canonical predictor writer unchanged only if the architecture and serving scorer are unchanged. Save the complete architecture configuration and strictly reload the selected checkpoint. Verify finite, matching evaluation scores across the trained module, ModelView and generated working/predict.py for short, full-length, truncated, mixed-length and singleton inputs. Serving retains intact observed histories and appended-mask inference; use the greatest nonpadding index, never nonpadding_count-1.

Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and the actual trained view.model. Preserve view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. Set dataset identity correctly. The diagnostic loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), each B x L. Measure positive–negative margins only at valid supervised positions and report terminal and interior subsets separately when their provenance is available. Use frozen diagnostic examples and negatives independent of training RNG. No ratings, review text, product categories, prices, stores or simulator traits are available; category breakdowns must remain unavailable. Diagnostic changes are descriptive and cannot replace host validation. User alignment=6/10: positive—addresses broad-match and stale-interest hypotheses; negative—cannot identify compatibility or present purpose. Model alignment=8/10: positive—directly trains candidate separation; negative—in-sample margin improvement need not improve HR@10.
idea.pseudocode:
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F


def final_nonpadding_index(sequence):
    """Works with LEFT padding and internal PAD holes; PAD=0."""
    if sequence.ndim != 2 or sequence.shape[1] == 0:
        raise ValueError('Expected a nonempty B x L sequence')
    positions = torch.arange(sequence.shape[1], device=sequence.device)
    last = positions.unsqueeze(0).expand_as(sequence).masked_fill(
        sequence.eq(0), -1
    ).amax(dim=1)
    if bool(last.lt(0).any()):
        raise ValueError('Empty terminal sequence')
    return last


def terminal_candidate_loss(model, sequence, target, negatives, mask_id,
                            score_fn=None):
    """One jointly trained BERT4Rec; no serving-time score fusion.

    sequence: B x L, leakage-free prefix ending in reserved MASK.
    target: B real item IDs.
    negatives: B x K unique eligible real IDs, PAD=0 only for shortages.
    Caller excludes each user's complete observed training-positive set.
    score_fn, when supplied: canonical differentiable (features, items)
      -> B x (K+1) logits, including any baseline scoring head.
    Otherwise this requires the baseline's canonical dot-product scorer.
    """
    if target.ndim != 1 or negatives.ndim != 2:
        raise ValueError('Invalid target/candidate dimensions')
    if sequence.shape[0] != target.shape[0] or negatives.shape[0] != target.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError('Batch dimensions differ')
    if not bool(((target > 0) & (target < mask_id)).all()):
        raise ValueError('Targets must be real items')
    if not bool(((negatives >= 0) & (negatives < mask_id)).all()):
        raise ValueError('Invalid negative IDs')
    valid_negative = negatives.ne(0)
    if not bool(valid_negative.any(dim=1).all()):
        raise ValueError('Each example needs an eligible negative')
    if bool((negatives.eq(target[:, None]) & valid_negative).any()):
        raise ValueError('Target included among negatives')
    ordered = negatives.sort(dim=1).values
    if bool((ordered[:, 1:].eq(ordered[:, :-1]) & ordered[:, 1:].ne(0)).any()):
        raise ValueError('Duplicate negative IDs')

    last = final_nonpadding_index(sequence)
    rows = torch.arange(sequence.shape[0], device=sequence.device)
    if not bool(sequence[rows, last].eq(mask_id).all()):
        raise ValueError('Terminal readout must be reserved MASK')
    if not bool(sequence.eq(mask_id).sum(dim=1).eq(1).all()):
        raise ValueError('Expected exactly one terminal MASK')

    features = model.log2feats(sequence)[rows, last]
    candidates = torch.cat((target[:, None], negatives), dim=1)
    if score_fn is None:
        logits = torch.einsum('bd,bkd->bk', features,
                              model.item_emb(candidates))
    else:
        logits = score_fn(features, candidates)
    if logits.shape != candidates.shape:
        raise ValueError('Canonical scorer returned incompatible shape')
    invalid = torch.cat((torch.zeros_like(target[:, None], dtype=torch.bool),
                         ~valid_negative), dim=1)
    logits = logits.float().masked_fill(invalid, float('-inf'))
    labels = torch.zeros(target.shape[0], dtype=torch.long,
                         device=target.device)
    return F.cross_entropy(logits, labels, reduction='mean')


# Integration specification; retain supplied baseline infrastructure:
# DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']
# For each of the four supplied categories, initialize ONE BERT4Rec with seed 42.
# For each configured epoch (<=200), perform exactly 200 baseline updates:
#   terminal, interior = supplied_corrected_sampler()
#   negatives = uniform_unique_eligible_training_only_candidates(K=32)
#   Lt = terminal_candidate_loss(model, terminal.sequence, terminal.target,
#                                negatives, MASK, canonical_score_fn)
#   Li = unchanged_baseline_interior_loss(model, interior)
#   loss = unchanged_alpha * Lt + (1 - unchanged_alpha) * Li
#   unchanged_optimizer_update(loss)
# Preserve supplied validation/checkpoint policy and diagnostic adapters.
# Export exactly one selected checkpoint per category with canonical writer.
# Host independently computes the fixed macro validation HR@10.

originality.positive: A narrowly specified terminal-only intervention separates candidate competition from architecture changes and the earlier dropout/curriculum directions.
originality.negative: Multi-negative sampled cross-entropy and terminal masked prediction are established techniques; this is an empirical adaptation rather than a new learning principle.

future_potential.positive: A successful controlled result could motivate later studies of candidate ambiguity and false-negative robustness within the same network.
future_potential.negative: Uniform candidates may remain easy, and exclusion or popularity effects may explain gains more readily than improved understanding of specific user needs.

code_difficulty.positive: Changes only a training loss and candidate sampler, adding no serving parameters or inference computation.
code_difficulty.negative: Efficient per-user exclusions, uniqueness, canonical scorer compatibility and diagnostic provenance require careful baseline integration.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer [1]
contributions: Introduces bidirectional masked-item learning for sequential recommendation.
Provides the backbone and masked-target formulation retained here.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed terminal-only 32-negative objective improves this pinned benchmark.

related_work.title: Sequential-recommendation negative-sampling comparison supplied in the search results [2]
contributions: The supplied summary reports dataset-dependent tradeoffs across random, popularity, in-batch and adaptive sampling.
limitations: Supports controlled sampling experiments rather than a universal advantage for harder negatives.
The supplied evidence does not establish gains under this task's fixed splits and candidates.

related_work.title: Pairwise Softmax Loss [3]
contributions: The supplied summary identifies false-negative sensitivity and proposes alternative pairwise activations.
limitations: The proposed experiment uses ordinary sampled cross-entropy and does not implement PSL.
False-negative robustness and benchmark gains cannot be inferred for the proposed loss.
